relevance_note: The paper describes four members of one family who underwent whole exome sequencing and states that "both his daughter and sister (both affected) were heterozygous for the VUS" in TNFAIP3, i.e. identifiable people with a TNFAIP3 variant (c.65G>A, p.R22Q), including one tested-negative relative.
method_note: The paper is a single-family case report with a pedigree figure (Figure 1) that carries no per-person labels, so no positional reading of the figure was attempted; all four sequenced family members (proband, his mother, his sister, his daughter) were extracted as separate rows, and the proband's deceased, untested father is kept as a relative described in relation to the proband. The paper prints no tables; no script transcribed anything, every span was copied by hand from the Markdown (some unit strings in the paper contain non-breaking spaces, so spans were trimmed to avoid them). Contradictions/notes: (1) the TNFAIP3 variant is called a 'variant of uncertain significance (VUS)' throughout, so no TNFAIP3 variant is attributed as causative; (2) an additional variant in GJB2 (c.35del, p.Gly12Valfs*2) is attributed to the proband and his mother only, so it is recorded only for them; (3) the abstract states the TNFAIP3 variant was found 'in all affected members', and the Results state the proband's mother was negative for it while his daughter and sister were heterozygous, so zygosity is left 'not reported' for the proband (no statement about his own genotype); (4) the GJB2 variant is described once as 'Another pathogenic variant' and once as 'The c.35delG variant inGJB2has been reported previously in association with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss', so no pathogenicity value is recorded for it; (5) the proband is reported as a '47-year-old Hispanic male' at the time of report but was 'initially referred to the Mayo Clinic at 34 years of age', so age_at_last_evaluation is 47 years and age_at_diagnosis is left not reported; (6) 'growth failure' was left 'not reported' for the 12-year-old daughter although she 'had to discontinue this activity due to swelling of her feet after practice' (gymnastics), because this is not an explicit statement about growth; (7) normal/negative findings were recorded per D-27: a normal CBC is written as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' excluded (an abnormal blood count is ruled out), while a normal bone marrow biopsy and 'serum protein electrophoresis that was within normal limits' are written as the paper does, because they name no single abnormality. Table/column note: no table is present, so no patient is shown as a table column and no stacked-cell issue arises. The paper states no total cohort size, so cohort_size_as_stated is null; n_patients_reported = 3 (the three family members with the TNFAIP3 variant).

treatment_summary.value: antihistamines (levocetirizine, cetirizine, fexofenadine, loratadine); prednisone and steroid injections cleared the hives but prednisone was stopped due to side effects; the paper suggests he may benefit from a trial of anti-IgE therapy (omalizumab)
span: The proband tried numerous treatment modalities to suppress his urticaria, including the following antihistamines: levocetirizine, cetirizine, fexofenadine, and loratadine.
Prednisone and steroid injections were the only treatments that cleared the patient's hives; however, treatment with prednisone was eventually stopped due to side effects.
The proband in this study had elevated tryptase and IgE levels, suggesting that he may benefit from a trial of this therapy in the future.

disease_label_as_stated.span: the patient did not meet diagnostic criteria for mastocytosis and was ultimately diagnosed with chronic urticaria.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: clinical evaluation excluding mastocytosis (bone marrow biopsy and CT scans) plus whole exome sequencing identifying a TNFAIP3 variant of uncertain significance
span: Due to the absence of mast cells in the bone marrow biopsy, the patient did not meet diagnostic criteria for mastocytosis and was ultimately diagnosed with chronic urticaria.
WES of the proband uncovered a novel variant inTNFAIP3 (Chr6(GRCh38): g.137871292G>A; NM_001270507.1: c.65G>A; p.(Arg22Gln)), which could possibly correlate with the proband's disease phenotype.
Bone marrow biopsy and computerized tomography (CT) scans ruled out visceral involvement by systemic mastocytosis, and the patient was later diagnosed with chronic urticaria.
